description: A `lat BETWEEN … AND lon BETWEEN …` query; a B-tree seeks on one column, so it walks a band around the planet and filters the rest.
Divides the Earth into cells with identifiers, so indexing a point is arithmetic and a location becomes an exact-match key.
Uber's open-source hexagonal hierarchical grid: 16 resolutions, each finer cell about one seventh of the area, with 64-bit integer cell ids.
All six neighbors of a hexagon are at the same distance from its center, while a square has edge and corner neighbors at two distances.
Every cell within `k` steps of a cell: 7 hexagons for `k = 1`, 19 for `k = 2`; the candidate set of a nearby query.
Counting available drivers and requests per cell id, used to set dynamic prices per area.
Domain-Oriented Microservice Architecture: services grouped into domains, domains into layers, each domain behind a gateway with extension points.
